course_name_original: Russian B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 2/3
course_name_en: Russian B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for first-cycle students - semester 2/3
prerequisites: Russian language at a minimum A2 level.

learning_outcomes.text: Can write understandable informative and argumentative texts on general and industry-specific topics, conduct correspondence typical for the work environment, and independently use didactic materials.
Can clearly present conclusions and opinions on general, academic, and professional topics in written and oral form.

Understands longer, even complex written and oral statements, e.g., lectures and presentations, provided they concern industry-specific issues and current affairs, and can interpret the acquired information.

Can use grammatical structures, phraseology, and vocabulary that allow understanding general texts describing contemporary economic and social phenomena, academic and industry-specific texts, and allow for fairly fluent and spontaneous communication in academic and professional environments.
Can prepare an oral presentation on academic and industry-specific topics and participate fairly fluently and spontaneously in discussions, also in a professional environment.

syllabus_topics: GRAMMAR ISSUES: Noun: accusative plural of animate nouns, neuter nouns ending in –мя, e.g., время (review), acronyms like турпоход, шоп-тур. Adjective: comparative degree, superlative degree with suffix –eйш-, -aйш- and with prefix най-, short form as predicate. Pronoun: negative with particles ни, не(-), e.g., ничего, нечего, indefinite with particles -то, -нибудь, e.g., кто-то, кто-нибудь. Verb: perfective, imperfective verbs (e.g., лететь - летать), imperative for 3rd person singular and plural and for 1st person plural, verbs of motion (куда? +Acc.) and state (где? +Loc.), adverbial and adjectival participles (active and passive), passive voice. Sentence constructions: cardinal number 2, 3, 4 + adjective + masculine or neuter noun. Translational attempts.

TOPICS AND VOCABULARY: University, studies, student life (Вуз, учёба, студенческая жизнь) - Education in Poland and Russia, university choice - Description of faculty and nature of studies. Future plans, career choice (Планы на будущее, выбор профессии) - Applying for a job - Ways for students to earn money. Dying and most prestigious professions (Исчезающие и престижные профессии) - Naming professions and describing professional activities. Job interview (Собеседование) - Ability to present oneself during an interview, dress code. Job offers in the press or on the Internet (Оферты работы, объявления) - Creating job advertisements, employment agency. Examples of formal letters, e.g., application, complaint, cover letter (Коммерческая корреспонденция) - Writing various forms of formal letters; business correspondence. Office equipment and supplies (Оргтехника) - Ordering office supplies, names of office equipment. Passport and visa formalities (Оформление визы) - Asking questions, providing information, writing invitations. Filling out forms, e.g., customs declaration (Как заполнить таможенную декларацию) - Types of customs and visa forms, blanks. Hotel room reservation (Бронировка номера в отеле) - Ability to book accommodation, tickets, etc. At the station, at the airport (Ha вокзалe, в аэропортy) - Most important places, e.g., waiting room, terminal, timetable; activities related to travel. Sport and tourism (Спорт и туризм) - Sports disciplines, pros and cons of playing sports - Sporting events and facilities. Health, doctor (Врач, болезнь) - Treatment, first aid - Medical specialties, medical supplies, etc. The environment we live in (Окружающая среда) - Ecological threats and environmental protection - Pro-ecological behaviors. We and culture (Мы и культурa) - Cultural events - Film, music, museum. Technology around us, Internet (Техника вокруг нас, Интернет) - Inventions, electronic devices, computer - Role of the Internet, etiquette rules on the Internet. Holidays and celebrations in Poland and Russia (Государственные и церковные праздники) - Holiday attributes, giving wishes.

LANGUAGE FUNCTIONS AND OTHER SKILLS: Conducting discussions – Проведение дискуссии. Commenting on information – Комментарии. Conducting conversations about everyday situations – Разговоры на бытовые темы. Giving advice – Советы. Expressing wishes – Желания. Forecasting – Прогнозирование. Stating reasons – Представление причин. Resolving conflicts, reacting in conflict situations. Conducting conversations about rules of conduct. Conducting short conversations with casually met people. Justifying one's position, presenting arguments 'for' and 'against', constructive criticism. Preparing and conducting a job interview. Filling out forms. Editing various types of texts: emails and private and official letters, e.g., cover letter, CV, letters to the editor, complaints, applications. Listening comprehension of interviews, general conversations, as well as popular science statements. Reading comprehension of popular science texts. Giving a presentation related to the field of study.
assessment_rules: A positive grade from all colloquiums conducted during the semester is required to pass. If a negative grade is received, the student has the right to improve it: improving a negative grade from the first attempt results in it being replaced by a positive grade counting towards the average, while improving a grade from the second attempt results in the average of the two grades being entered. The average partial grade, if the test is passed, cannot be less than 3.0. Unjustified absence from a test results in loss of the attempt; students are entitled to two retake colloquiums with intervals of no less than 2 days. The final grade for the language course is the arithmetic average of all grades obtained from passing individual semesters and the foreign language exam. Admission to the exam requires passing the compulsory language course semesters.
